original_value: Flying ad hoc network (FANET) is a self-organizing wireless network that enables inexpensive, flexible, and easy-to-deploy flying nodes, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), to communicate among themselves in the absence of fixed network infrastructure. FANET is one of the emerging networks that has an extensive range of next-generation applications. Hence, FANET plays a significant role in achieving application-based goals. Routing enables the flying nodes to collaborate and coordinate among themselves and to establish routes to radio access infrastructure, particularly FANET base station (BS). With a longer route lifetime, the effects of link disconnections and network partitions reduce. Routing must cater to two main characteristics of FANETs that reduce the route lifetime. Firstly, the collaboration nature requires the flying nodes to exchange messages and to coordinate among themselves, causing high energy consumption. Secondly, the mobility pattern of the flying nodes is highly dynamic in a three-dimensional space and they may be spaced far apart, causing link disconnection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the limited research work of routing schemes in FANETs. Different aspects, including objectives, challenges, routing metrics, characteristics, and performance measures, are covered. Furthermore, we present open issues.

result.paraphrase: A flying ad hoc network (FANET) is a self-organizing wireless network that allows low-cost, flexible, and easy-to-deploy flying nodes, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), to communicate with one another without fixed network infrastructure. FANET is among the emerging networks with a broad set of next-generation applications, and it therefore plays an important role in meeting application-specific goals. Routing helps flying nodes cooperate and coordinate with each other and set up routes to radio access infrastructure, especially a FANET base station (BS). Longer route lifetimes lessen the impact of link failures and network partitions. Routing must address two key FANET properties that shorten route lifetime. First, the collaborative nature of the nodes requires them to exchange messages and coordinate, which leads to high energy consumption. Second, the nodes move in a highly dynamic three-dimensional space and may be widely separated, resulting in link disconnections. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey of the limited research on routing schemes in FANETs. We cover multiple aspects, including objectives, challenges, routing metrics, characteristics, and performance measures. We also discuss open issues.
